blocks.text:
Whenever you press or release a key, an event is emitted. You can add an
event controller and connect a signal handler to handle such events.

The event signal handler will receive arguments that depend on the type of event.
For key press events the arguments are (guint keyval,
guint keycode, Gdk::ModifierType state).
As described in the appendix,
the key press event signal handler returns a bool value, to indicate that
the signal is fully handled (true) or allow event propagation
(false).

To determine which key was pressed or released, you read the value of
the keyval argument and compare it with a constant in the

<gdk/gdkkeysyms.h> header file. The states of
modifier keys (shift, ctrl, etc.) are available as bit-flags in
state.

In this example there are three keyboard shortcuts:
Alt+1 selects the first radio button,
Alt+2 selects the second one, and the
Esc key closes the window.
